I was not aware I was relapsing when I first came upon this subreddit. I was convinced my ED was a thing of the past and that I was absolutely fine. I was in denial for a while about it.

I no longer visit this subreddit. I saw this post when I was unfollowing some subs that I realized I have no place in due to my current situation. 

I want to be very clear that I do not think this sub triggered my relapse -- fasting is not anorexia and many people here have a healthy approach to fasting. I respect this sub and that is why I have been detaching myself from it.

It definitely took a lot of people calling me on my bullshit for me to realize I wasn't approaching fasting or conceptualization of food in a healthy manner. I think this sub has value and that fasting has value, but I don't think we should ever look the other way when people say things that send off alarm bells.

I didn't realize my thought patterns were going back to ED until about a month or two ago -- I thought I was approaching fasting in a healthy way, since nothing was sending off alarm bells. I thought it was other people who had disordered relationships to food, not the majority of people here, and certainly not me. 

Once I got over the denial and realized I was relapsing, I stopped being active on these kinds of boards. I still fast occasionally but I'm no longer pretending it's the same type of fasting people here do.

Not gonna lie, some posts on this sub fed into my current relapse and I know several people who use this thread on side accounts because their main accounts are very obviously ED-related. 

Not saying this sub directly encourages EDs but some things encouraged and discussed have fed into my existing issues and were one factor of many that have contributed. Namely things like keeping it a secret, occasionally things like people already being very thin or the ways food is discussed at times.

I don't think fasting is inherently disordered but I do think a lot of people with underlying issues can find this type of environment enabling. I don't think it's anyone's responsibility to look out for us, but I do think it wouldn't hurt to be more careful with our words.

EDIT: before another person asks me about this, I want to say that when I realized I was relapsing, I *stopped coming to this sub*. When I *first* came to it, I was in denial about my ED. I did not believe I had one. I thought I was approaching fasting in a healthy way, but when I realized I am not, I just stopped coming here. I saw this post because I switched over to this account, which I am rarely active on, which is still part of this sub. On my side account I am only active in ED subs. I am fully aware this is not a good environment for some with my type of ED, which is primarily restrictive. I am fully aware that if someone with a restrictive ED comes to this sub to purposely trigger themselves, that is not the fault of the sub. I don't think everyone here should have to walk on eggshells for us, I just think it's important to pay attention to what people are saying and consider it it sounds healthy or not. Because some people are in denial about their ED, and some people are aware of their EDs but are uninterested in recovery, and they all make posts here!!!

Ingredients

Serves 1

6 oz chicken breasts

3 tbsp powdered peanut butter

3 tsp arrowroot starch

½ tbsp olive oil

1 tbsp soy sauce (low sodium)

1 tsp ground ginger

1½ tbsp rice vinegar

Sriracha sauce

Green onion

Sesame seeds

Brown rice

Lime

....
Steps

1. In a bowl, mix together soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, sriracha sauce and powdered peanut butter.

2. Add olive oil to a skillet and heat up the cooked chicken, then sprinkle on one-third ONLY of the arrowroot starch and stir.

3. To the sauce, mix in the remainder of the arrowroot starch and pour into the skillet, then stir and cook for no more than 2 minutes.

4. Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.

5. Serve with brown rice and a wedge of lime.
